summary: The latest screened arXiv window is strongest on intermediate-mass dilepton thermometry, statistically validated heavy-ion calorimeter inpainting, interpretable generator-systematics decompositions, and efficient transformer jet tagging. The direct heavy-ion theory highlight is arXiv:2608.16102, which clarifies why dilepton inverse slopes track an emission-weighted harmonic temperature while warning that the mapping is nonuniversal. The most practical physics-AI/ML result is arXiv:2608.14801 because it evaluates uncertainty calibration and spatial bias for detector inpainting rather than relying on generic generative-model quality metrics.
strongest_paper: 2608.16102: Origin and limits of intermediate-mass dilepton thermometry
top_takeaway: Dilepton thermometry and validation-focused detector AI are the strongest signals; broader HEP-ML papers are useful where they expose model differences, reduce compute cost, or keep topology reconstruction uncertainty visible.

papers.title: Origin and limits of intermediate-mass dilepton thermometry
papers.abstract: Controlled expanding-fireball study showing that intermediate-mass dilepton inverse slopes track an emission-weighted harmonic mean of source temperatures while remaining nonuniversal under changes in cooling history or source composition.

papers.title: Statistical validation of calorimeter inpainting with generative diffusion priors
papers.abstract: Bayesian heavy-ion calorimeter inpainting with diffusion priors, evaluated through energy response, spatial bias, uncertainty calibration, centrality, and mask-size diagnostics.

papers.title: Functional anatomy of Pythia-Herwig differences with Kolmogorov-Arnold networks
papers.abstract: KAN decomposition of classifier-derived log density ratios identifies which jet-observable components drive Pythia-Herwig differences across generator stages.

papers.title: Assessing Parameter Redundancy in Transformers for Jet Tagging
papers.authors_short: Huitong Cheng, Yabo Dong, Jun Fan, Kun Wang, Haijun Yang, Jingya Zhu, Yifan Zhu
papers.abstract: Hourglass feed-forward blocks and lightweight embeddings reduce ParT/MIParT parameter counts while retaining most top-tagging and quark-gluon discrimination performance.

papers.title: Pairton: Iterative Reconstruction of Short-Lived Particles
papers.authors_short: Andreas Hermansen, Chris Scheulen, Tobias Golling
papers.abstract: Iterative masked graph-prediction framework for short-lived particle reconstruction, demonstrated on fully hadronic top-pair decays.

papers.title: Uncovering Hidden Leptonic Correlations with Flow Matching and Autoencoders
papers.authors_short: Haruto Kitagawa, Satsuki Nishimura, Hajime Otsuka
papers.abstract: Flow matching and autoencoders are used to explore Type-I seesaw parameter correlations, but the abstract-level evidence does not yet establish robust physical interpretability or transfer value.

screening.selection_rationale: Abstract-first triage selected direct heavy-ion papers and physics AI/ML papers with concrete HEP or nuclear transfer value; loosely related phenomenology and generic ML papers were omitted.
